title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Labour and Social Security continues to support the implementation of Workplace Adaptation Programme (WAP) in Türkiye in collaboration with employer organisations and the ILO, to advance decent work measures and social cohesion. WAP equips refugee and host community workers with knowledge of workplace norms and rights, gender equality, and anti-discrimination measures while fostering social cohesion and peace in the workplace, reflecting the international labour standards, particularly R.205. The effectiveness of the programme was assessed and relying on the results, new modules on people with disabilities, awareness on trade union rights and prevention of mobbing and harassment at the workplace are included within the programme.
Following the devastating earthquakes of 6 February 2023, the Government of Turkiye in collaboration with UN agencies prepared and adopted Türkiye Earthquakes Recovery and Reconstruction Assessment (TERRA) and started to implement employment and decent work measures to tackle the effects of the earthquakes in the labour market. ILO coordinated the drafting of the Employment section of TERRA and integrated the Fundamental Principles and Right at Work and Recommendation 205. Through the WAP, ILO contributed to establishing a harmonious work atmosphere, benefiting refugees and local workers. With an aim to improve the implementation of the programme, the ILO adopted both qualitative and quantitative assessment tools, using tailor made Attitudes and Knowledge Scale, empirical data from ILO consultants. Relying on the results of the assessment, the outcomes of WAP was analysed and the content of the programme was scaled-up. This initiative further facilitated refugees' integration into the workforce and strengthen the institutional capacity of employers' organisations, enabling them to support their members in fostering workplace peace and stability. Almost 1.000 workers benefitted from WAP in this biennium, which is implemented in close cooperation with the employers’ organisations and brands such as H&M and Inditex, with the funding from United States Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration. The ILO Office for Türkiye has worked intensively with the government institutions, social partners and development partners to rapidly convert some activities of existing projects into emergency aid by funding from German Development Bank (KfW), European Union, FERRERO, CAOBISCO and SIDA. Containers have been provided to the regional offices of the ISKUR (Turkish Employment Agency) to ensure that the services are not disrupted. A report named “The effects of the February 2023 earthquake on the labour market in Türkiye” was published. First-hand aid to the earthquake-affected region, such as winter tents, sleeping bags, pillows, clothing sets, hygiene boxes, hot meals and food parcels for children and adult distributed, prioritizing seasonal agricultural workers and their families as well as the refugees. Moreover, psycho-social support activities are being conducted. Several portable bathrooms and WCs established in response to the daily needs of the earthquake survivals in the region.

description.narrative: The Regional Employment Offices under İstanbul Metropolitan Municipality, in collaboration with the ILO implemented right-based career counselling training programme with an aim to enhance the capacity of employment and career centres as well as the counsellors employed in municipalities to provide rights-based career counselling and job-matching services in fragile settings. A series of capacity-building activities, grounded in ILO Convention No. 181 and Recommendation No. 188, improved the service delivery towards vulnerable groups, including refugees and host community members with a focus on youth, women and people with disabilities. By fostering service improvement for vulnerable groups, including refugees and host community members, we have driven essential change in local labour markets. The innovative approach to developing multilingual materials ensured the broader accessibility and inclusivity of our services. Partnerships with municipalities have been instrumental, allowing the ILO to contribute to providing sustainable, decentralised, more accessible services. Programme’s holistic approach reflects the ILO's commitment to promoting decent work for all, particularly migrant workers and refugees, in line with the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.

description.narrative: The work-based-learning (WBL) programme, that was designed in collaboration with the Ministry of Labour and Social Security was “scaled-up” based on lessons learned from the pilot phase conducted in one province, whereby modifications were adopted to improve the initial approach. The WBL programme was expanded to six provinces, where the municipalities and organised industrial zones are implementing in collaboration with the ILO. The programme aims to develop the skills of employees through on-the-job trainings, support decent work opportunities for women, youth and persons with disabilities and contribute to the meeting market needs for qualified labour. The programme also includes trainings on fundamental principles, rights and obligations at work, ILO standards, core employability skills, occupational safety and health and gender equality. 2.116 individuals supported through this program. The ILO contributed by allocating monthly wage subsidies, monthly reimbursement of social security premiums, additional financial support for women and persons with disabilities, childcare services support for women and one-time work permit fee reimbursement for refugee trainees with the financial support of the German Development Bank (KfW). Among the 2,116 beneficiaries, a total of 307 beneficiaries worked less than 40 days. Among these 311 beneficiaries, 55 of them continue to work. 1,809 short-term employment beneficiaries worked more than 40 days at the companies where they were placed as WBL trainees. WBL programme supported 693 women and 91 persons with disabilities. 908 refugees were reached by the WBL programme and social cohesion among the refugees and host communities also supported. The ILO conducted an extensive field survey with the objective of identifying the underlying reasons behind the dropout cases.
